title: High-Throughput Multi Well Plate Approach for Recombinant Protein Assay
author: Baker, Mulvihill

steps.title: Grow E. coli in multi-well plates
steps.instruction: Inoculate E. coli carrying the VNp‑fusion construct into multi‑well plates and incubate under appropriate growth conditions; induce protein expression at the recommended time point for your system.

steps.title: Harvest vesicles from culture
steps.instruction: Separate vesicles from the cells either by centrifugation or by filtration:

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate for 5 min to pellet cells, then carefully transfer the vesicle‑containing supernatant to a fresh multi‑well plate (choose plate type suitable for downstream assay, e.g., black wells or UV‑transparent wells).
Alternatively, pass the culture through a multi‑well filter that retains cells while allowing vesicles to flow through into a fresh plate.

steps.title: Store or proceed with vesicle samples
steps.instruction: The plate containing vesicle samples can be stored long‑term at 4 °C or used immediately for downstream steps.

steps.title: Lyse vesicles with non‑ionic detergent
steps.instruction: Add a non‑ionic detergent such as Triton X‑100 or Tween to each well to lyse vesicles and release the recombinant protein into the medium; perform this step only if the assay substrate cannot cross the lipid membrane.

steps.title: Optional in‑plate affinity purification
steps.instruction: If >80 % protein purity is required, apply an in‑plate affinity‑tag purification protocol to the lysate to isolate the protein of interest.

steps.title: Perform downstream fluorescence/absorbance assay
steps.instruction: Use the purified or crude protein directly in fluorescence, absorbance, or enzymatic assays as needed; the protocol supports high‑throughput measurement of signal changes in multi‑well format.
